assertion_analysis.failure_condition: Revert the fingerprint comparison in definitions_unchanged (the declared negative control): the rewritten _compute_refresh assertion at line 99 reddens because _stored_discovery returns the stored dict instead of None; observed in negative-control.log (assert {...} is None -> AssertionError, EXIT=1). Remove the file-revision memo: len(source_reads) == 1 at line 86 reddens (two reads). Revert _refresh_main's fingerprint recording: line 66 raises KeyError on payload['source_fingerprints']. Revert the read's fingerprints branch to the source_revision comparison: line 63 reddens, because the child stored source_revision None while the parent's _SOURCE_SNAPSHOT.revision is monkeypatched to 'new-process'. These assertions compare production output against test-side expectations (a spawn list, None-ness, a read count), independent of the values under test.

assert stored[0] == payload['result'] compares _refresh_result's return against the same store file's content, so both sides read the one JSON the code wrote; it reddens only if _refresh_result stops returning the stored result and is not by itself a guard for the fingerprint path. The discriminating assertions for this change are lines 63, 86, 95-100.

findings.text: follow-on: definitions_unchanged returns True for an empty recorded mapping, and the read at reckon/route_results.py:126 tests `fingerprints is not None` rather than its truth, so a stored result whose fingerprint map is empty is served indefinitely even after the deriving code changes. The map is empty only when the child's ExecutedSource recorded no definition (definition_fingerprints returns {} from an empty _used_definitions), which the child's own start() guard makes unlikely, so this is a fail-open edge rather than a live defect; a stricter read would treat an empty map as unverifiable.
